mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate compresses the risk-free rate in equity valuation models, increasing present values of future cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%, as measured by a rolling 3-year window with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0, as measured by a rolling 3-year window with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being negative.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high federal funds rate (above 4.5%) and high unemployment rate (above 5.0%) indicates stagflation, compressing corporate profit margins and increasing risk aversion, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5 AND UNRATE > 5.0, as measured by a rolling 3-year window with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being negative.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, declining housing starts (HOUST below 2100.0) signal weakening residential demand that precedes broader economic slowdowns, reducing corporate earnings expectations and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST declines by more than 1.0% month-over-month, as measured by a rolling 3-year window with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being negative.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 108.0 signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days through immediate market reaction to supply-side weakness.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 108.0, as measured by a rolling 3-year window with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being negative.

mechanism_narrative: Robust retail sales above 350,000 million dollars (RSAFS > 350000) indicate strong consumer demand that supports corporate revenue growth, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through sustained earnings momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 350000, as measured by a rolling 3-year window with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being positive.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of non-farm payrolls above 134,000 thousand (PAYEMS > 134000) indicates a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through sustained economic momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS > 134000, as measured by a rolling 3-year window with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being positive.

mechanism_narrative: A high consumer price index above 200.0 (CPIAUCSL > 200.0) signals accelerating inflation that prompts Federal Reserve tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 200.0, as measured by a rolling 3-year window with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being negative.
